# RecenterWatch

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/RecenterWatch.cs#L31)

A watch worn on one wrist that the other hand holds a finger on to put the player back where
they belong. Hold for [`holdSeconds`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/RecenterWatch#holdseconds) and it plays its sound and recenters the player
on the last recenter point used - the one the Interaction module remembers - so wherever the
scene last put them is where they go.

Its own script rather than a [`TriggerStay`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/TriggerStay) wired up by events, because the
trigger stay matches on a name or a tag and a hand is neither: it is four sets of colliders
on two layers, and the one that matters is "the hand this is not worn on". That is asked of
[`HandParts`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/HandParts), so the wearing hand's own fingers curling past the face never
count.

Touch is read from the physics step rather than kept from enter and exit events: every step
a part of the other hand overlaps the face marks it touched, and the next step reads and
clears the mark. A fingertip that is disabled, re-parented or destroyed while on the watch
sends no exit, and a count kept from exits ran on with nothing touching it.

Worn under the visual hand's wrist bone, not under the visual hand's root. The root of a
visual hand never moves - the solver places its wrist bone on the physics hand and the mesh
follows the bones - so a watch parented to the root stays on the floor where the rig was
spawned. That was the first thing wrong with the one this replaces.

### Step(float) {#step-single}

the count, and completes it once it has run for [`holdSeconds`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/RecenterWatch#holdseconds).

### Touch(Collider) {#touch-collider}

Marks the face touched for this physics step, if the collider is part of the pressing hand.
What the trigger callback feeds in; on its own so something other than the physics can stand
in for it.
